\title{\textbf{Stages 1 and 2: the frozen models, 4B against 8B}}
\author{}
\date{2026-11-01}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\noindent
Stages~1 and~2 put the brief in front of a frozen language model, with no
training, and score the controller it writes exactly as training will score
it. Stage~1 gives the model one turn: the brief without the probe section,
and the controller straight away. Stage~2 gives it the two-turn protocol: an
optional probe run on a throwaway batch, whose printed output comes back to
it, then the controller. This document compares two models on the same
batches, \texttt{Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507}, the base the training stages use,
and \texttt{Qwen3-8B} in non-thinking mode, twice its size from the same
generation. Both are read against the references Stage~0 fixed on the same
held-out tasks.

\paragraph{Terms.} A \emph{sample} is one rollout on one task at the sampling
temperature. \emph{Valid} means the reply held a controller that passed
validation (a \texttt{def policy(state)} with only the allowed imports).
\emph{Success} and \emph{fast success} are the environment's own outcome and
success within $1.25\times$ the oracle's steps; \emph{normalised time} is
oracle steps over own steps, zero on failure. The \emph{ride ratio} is the
highest reported $\sigma$ of the final run divided by the batch's limit: one
is the oracle, lower is caution, above one is a shower. The \emph{probe rate}
is the share of Stage~2 samples whose first reply was probe code rather than
a controller. The \emph{estimate error} is how far the number closest to the
true limit in the probe's printed output lies from it. \emph{Cut off} means
the reply opened a code block the token budget closed before it ended.
\emph{Ruined} is a shower or lost seeds; \emph{error} is a controller that
did not run, scored at the error floor.

\section{Protocol}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
  \item \textbf{Tasks.} The \SFntasks\ held-out tasks of
  \texttt{crystallizer\_eval.jsonl}, 16 per third of the limit's range, the
  same batches as Stage~0's references.
  \item \textbf{Samples.} \SFnsamples\ per task per run at temperature $0.8$,
  top-$p$ $0.95$, at most \SFmaxtokens\ new tokens per turn.
  \item \textbf{Brief.} The brief of the paper's appendix, with the two quench
  logs and the stated range of the limit; Stage~1 without the probe section.
  \item \textbf{Models.} \texttt{Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507} (instruct-only, no
  thinking mode) and \texttt{Qwen3-8B} with thinking switched off through the
  chat template's \texttt{enable\_thinking=False}, as its model card
  instructs; bf16 weights, one A30 each, no gradient updates.
  \item \textbf{Scoring.} The runner's sandbox: the probe run on the probe
  batch with the limit masked, the controller on the scoring batch,
  \texttt{score\_sample} as the trainer uses it.
  \item \textbf{References.} The cautious blind controller and the oracle of
  Stage~0, on the same tasks.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Reading}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
  \item \textbf{Both frozen models sit far below the cautious blind
  reference.} The 4B base scores $-84$ in one turn and $-66$ with the
  two-turn protocol; the 8B scores $-207$ and $-192$. The cautious blind
  controller, which never probes and never fails, scores $+38$; the oracle
  $+80$; the hand-written probe run and controller of Stage~0, $+77$. No run
  reaches fast success on more than one sample in a hundred. The headroom for
  training is the whole scale.

  \item \textbf{The 8B is worse than the 4B on every column, and the reason
  is in Table~\ref{tab:errors}:} 91 and 90 of its 192 samples never run. Its
  controllers use \texttt{L} without reading it from the state or refer to an
  \texttt{initial\_L} they never set (49 undefined names in Stage~1); they
  read \texttt{state['done']} although the brief states that \texttt{done} is
  returned by \texttt{env.step} and the flags are attributes of \texttt{env}
  (7 crashes in Stage~1, 33 in Stage~2); and in Stage~2 they call \texttt{env}
  inside the controller although the brief states the controller has no
  access to it (37 controllers contain \texttt{env.step} or
  \texttt{env.reset}, 21 crash on it). In non-thinking mode the 8B writes
  longer, more elaborate code with more invented names. The 4B's errors are
  almost all replies the token budget cut off mid-code (16 of 22 in Stage~1).

  \item \textbf{Neither model uses the probe run.} 12 and 11 first replies of
  192 are probe code, and every one of them was cut off by the 1000-token
  budget: the sandbox rejected the unfinished block, the model received the
  rejection as its probe output, and wrote the controller without a
  measurement. No probe output holds a number within $0.01$ of the limit,
  so the estimate-error column is empty and the Stage~2 ride ratios carry
  nothing a probe found. The probe replies run from 2\,563 to 4\,430
  characters (Table~\ref{tab:diagnostics}), past the budget; the frozen
  probe rate is measured with the budget as a confound.

  \item \textbf{For the 4B, the two-turn protocol helps at inference only by
  shortening the reply.} Reward rises from $-84$ to $-66$ because cut-off
  replies fall from $17.7\%$ to $3.6\%$ (median reply 2\,999 characters in
  Stage~1, 2\,086 in Stage~2), while success falls from
  $27\%$ to $23\%$ and fast success to zero.

  \item \textbf{Where the samples succeed} (Table~\ref{tab:by-third}): the
  4B succeeds on about half the high-third batches and on one in twenty to
  thirty of the low third. It cools at a fixed moderate rate that high limits
  tolerate and low limits punish: 93 and 132 batches ruined, and a mean ride
  ratio of $0.75$ to $0.79$ that averages over-riding low limits with
  under-riding high ones. The 8B mostly times out (51 and 31 of 192): it
  cools too slowly or stops; its ride ratio is $0.30$ to $0.50$.

  \item \textbf{The superseded first round agrees within sampling noise}
  (4B $-85$ and $-53$, 8B $-209$ and $-195$; the provenance comments in the
  source of this document name that round), so the sandbox bug floored
  twelve samples but did not shape the picture.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{For the ladder.} The 4B base remains the model to train: the 8B
gives no better start at twice the memory. ``Whether to probe'' has a frozen
baseline of about six percent, and at 1000 tokens per turn no probe the
frozen models write fits; raising the budget, or measuring the probe rate at
a budget where a probe can run, is a protocol decision to take before the
training stages, not one this document takes.


\section{Reproduce}
\sloppy
% commits and jobs: see the provenance block at the top of this file
The weights: \texttt{hf download Qwen/Qwen3-8B --local-dir
models/hf\_base/qwen3-8b} on the cluster's run node (the 4B base is at
\texttt{models/hf\_base/iter\_000}). Each run is one job:
\begin{scriptsize}
\begin{verbatim}
hpc submit lora4vr jobs/hpi/stage1.sbatch --job-name=stage1-8b \
    --export=ALL,LORA4VR_GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD),MODEL_PATH=models/hf_base/qwen3-8b,N_SAMPLES=4
hpc submit lora4vr jobs/hpi/stage2.sbatch --job-name=stage2-8b \
    --export=ALL,LORA4VR_GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD),MODEL_PATH=models/hf_base/qwen3-8b,N_SAMPLES=4
hpc pull lora4vr/results/stage2-8b_<jobid> docs/stage12/
uv run python scripts/frozen_render.py --out docs/stage12/tables \
    stage1-4b=docs/stage12/stage1-4b_<jobid> stage2-4b=docs/stage12/stage2-4b_<jobid> \
    stage1-8b=docs/stage12/stage1-8b_<jobid> stage2-8b=docs/stage12/stage2-8b_<jobid>
\end{verbatim}
\end{scriptsize}
and the same with \texttt{MODEL\_PATH=models/hf\_base/iter\_000} for the 4B
runs. Each result directory holds the job log, \texttt{stage<N>\_summary.json}
with its provenance block and per-task rows, and
\texttt{stage<N>\_samples.jsonl} with every sample: the full transcript, the
probe code, the tool output, the controller and its outcome.
